issues.description: `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` is gratuitously clever and obscures intent in the Basic Usage example
issues.detail: The Basic Usage block uses `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` to retrieve the only node. This is equivalent to `pipeline.nodes[0]` but harder to read, and worse, it pretends a single-node pipeline is the general case — a reader copying it into a multi-node pipeline will silently get some other node. Replace with `pipeline.nodes[0]` or filter explicitly by name (`next(n for n in pipeline.nodes if n.name == 'train_model_node')`).

issues.description: `node(...)` snippets appear as bare top-level expressions outside any `Pipeline([...])` and are not runnable as shown
issues.detail: Several later code blocks (Mermaid customisation, Text-with-syntax-highlighting, the closure / `make_preview_fn` examples) show `node(func=..., preview_fn=..., name=...)` as a free-floating statement with no surrounding pipeline and no assignment. A reader copy-pasting these will produce code that has no effect. Either embed each call inside a `Pipeline([...])` literal as the first example does, or annotate clearly that these are fragments.

issues.description: `meta` field is overloaded with two distinct responsibilities — general metadata and renderer configuration
issues.detail: The docs explicitly state that `meta` serves both as freeform contextual info (timestamps, versions) and as load-bearing rendering configuration (Mermaid layout, syntax-highlighting language). These are two unrelated contracts sharing one untyped dict, with no precedence rule, no reserved-key list per subtype, and no collision policy. Either split into two fields (e.g., `meta` vs `render_config`), reserve a namespace, or at minimum document the reserved keys and their precedence per preview subtype.

issues.description: Closure-for-data-context example silently teaches a frozen-literal pattern that pretends to be live data
issues.detail: The 'Use closure to capture context' example bakes a hard-coded `sample_data` literal into `preview_fn` at pipeline-construction time. The preview will not reflect runtime catalog state, but the prose presents this as the way to preview 'actual data', and the same section also promises that preview functions can 'access datasets within the preview function' without showing how. State the temporal contract explicitly (closure captures build-time values, not run-time facts) and either deliver the dataset-access pattern or drop the claim.

issues.description: Lifecycle and contract of `preview_fn` and `node.preview()` are unspecified
issues.detail: The docs never state the contract behind the new extension point: when `preview_fn` is invoked (eagerly, lazily on `.preview()`, on each viz refresh), whether it must be pure / deterministic / side-effect-free, what `node.preview()` returns when `preview_fn` is unset, whether exceptions propagate or are wrapped, and whether `to_dict()` is part of the supertype contract. Without these invariants, every consumer and user implementation will guess differently. State preconditions, postconditions, error semantics, and call-frequency before this graduates from experimental.

issues.description: Best-practice item 5 ('Handle errors: wrap preview logic in try-except if needed') is vague and substitutes etiquette for contract
issues.detail: Telling readers to wrap preview logic in try/except 'if needed' is symptomatic of a missing contract. The docs do not say what exceptions are anticipated, whether kedro swallows or propagates them, whether a failed preview breaks the node run, or what to return on failure. Either specify the failure mode (e.g., `preview_fn` exceptions are caught and surfaced as a typed error payload) or drop the bullet — vague safety advice trains readers to swallow errors rather than reason about them.

issues.description: PR checklist admits no tests and no RELEASE.md entry for a new user-facing surface
issues.detail: The PR checklist leaves both 'Added tests' and 'Added RELEASE.md entry' unchecked. For a docs-only PR the test omission is defensible, but documenting a new public surface (`preview_fn` kwarg, `preview_contract` module, `node.preview()`) without a RELEASE.md note means downstream users will not be told the feature exists. Add the RELEASE.md entry under the appropriate experimental-features section, and ideally anchor at least one snippet to a doctest so the docs track the implementation.

issues.description: ImagePreview example uses an unconditional `return` followed by a commented-out alternative — misleading pedagogy
issues.detail: The Image preview function has `return ImagePreview(content="https://...")` followed by a commented-out data-URI alternative inside the same function. The structure implies a function can do both, when it cannot. Split into two named functions (one per transport mode), matching the Option 1 / Option 2 pattern used in the Table preview section.

issues.description: Lowercase `polars` added to Vale `ignore.txt` alongside existing `Polars` without explanation
issues.detail: `Polars` is already on the ignore list; adding lowercase `polars` is fine but unexplained. Either fix the underlying prose (Polars is a proper noun) or document in the commit why a lowercase variant is needed (e.g., it appears inside a code-shaped phrase like `df.head(5).to_dicts()`). Quietly duplicating an entry in two cases is the kind of style-config drift that compounds.

issues.description: ImagePreview accepts URL or data URI through one untyped `content` field with no discriminator
issues.detail: ImagePreview.content can be either an external URL or an inline base64 data URI, distinguished only by string prefix. These are semantically different (a reference to a remote, mutable place vs. an inline value frozen at preview time) with different trust, caching, and time semantics. Either add an explicit `kind` discriminator or document the prefix-sniffing rule as the contract so every renderer behaves identically.

issues.description: MermaidPreview `meta` example mixes Mermaid-native config with Kedro-Viz-specific keys (e.g., `textStyle`) with no distinction flagged
issues.detail: The `custom_config` example places `securityLevel`, `flowchart`, and `themeVariables` (real Mermaid config) alongside `textStyle`, which is not in the Mermaid schema and appears to be a Kedro-Viz frontend rendering concern. The footnote links to the Mermaid schema as if all keys are pass-through. Document precisely which keys are Mermaid-native, which are Kedro-Viz extensions, and what happens to unknown keys — and prefer linking to the upstream schema over hand-mirrored `(default: X)` annotations that will drift.

issues.description: CustomPreview `renderer_key` has no contract for namespacing, collision, or unknown-key handling
issues.detail: CustomPreview is the explicit extension point but the docs say only that `renderer_key` 'identifies which frontend component should handle rendering'. Missing: who owns the key namespace, how collisions with built-in renderers are avoided, what a consumer does on an unrecognised key (ignore, fallback to text, error), and whether `content` is validated or opaque pass-through. Without this contract the extension point will fragment across users and break Kedro-Viz forward compatibility.

issues.description: Experimental warning links via a relative path that may break across docs builds
issues.detail: The warning admonition links to `../about/experimental.md`. Relative links inside MkDocs admonitions are fragile across navigation depth and file relocation; the link can rot silently. Use a canonical docs URL or a MkDocs-resolved cross-reference and verify it renders correctly.

issues.description: TextPreview `meta.language` accepted values and fallback behaviour are under-documented
issues.detail: The doc lists `python`, `javascript`, and `yaml` as supported highlighting languages but does not say what happens for unsupported values — silent fallback to plain text, error, raw output. One short sentence on the fallback behaviour closes the gap for users writing `meta={'language': 'sql'}`.

issues.description: Table preview helpers take a DataFrame argument despite the explicit statement that preview functions receive no inputs
issues.detail: The Table preview section presents `def preview_from_dataframe(df: pd.DataFrame) -> TablePreview` and `def preview_from_polars(df) -> TablePreview` as if they could be passed to `preview_fn=`. The docs later state plainly that preview functions don't have access to node inputs or outputs and are invoked with no arguments by `node.preview()`. Rewrite these as zero-arg closures (matching the later closure pattern) or explicitly label them as helpers that must be wrapped.

issues.description: Module boundary between kedro core and kedro-viz is blurred in the preview docs
issues.detail: The `preview_contract` module sits in `kedro.pipeline`, but the documented contract is dominated by what Kedro-Viz does with the payload (renderer_key conventions, language highlighting, Mermaid config merging with 'sensible defaults', textStyle CSS). This couples the two repos at the spec level and means the kedro contract changes every time the viz frontend changes. Draw the line: kedro promises the payload shape; kedro-viz documents how it renders. At minimum, name which surfaces are likely to change as the feature evolves out of experimental.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a docs-only PR introducing user-facing documentation for an experimental `preview_fn` feature, and that the prose is generally clear and well-structured. The dominant criticism across reviewers is that the documentation does not state the contract behind the feature: when `preview_fn` runs, what state it may observe, what `node.preview()` returns / raises, and whether the function must be pure. Several code snippets fail their own stated contract — gratuitous `next(...)` over `pipeline.nodes`, bare `node(...)` calls outside any pipeline, Table-preview helpers that take a DataFrame argument despite the explicit no-inputs rule, and an ImagePreview function with unreachable code after `return`. The `meta` field openly serves two distinct jobs (user metadata and renderer config), and the Mermaid example leaks Kedro-Viz frontend concerns through what reads as Mermaid pass-through. NEEDS-WORK before this becomes the reference page: state the lifecycle/contract, fix the non-runnable snippets, separate meta from render config (or document the precedence), and add a RELEASE.md entry.
